name: Lunar Roving Vehicle
dispatch: The Lunar Rover was the first car on another world, and its entire reason to exist was reach. On foot, an astronaut can't stray far from the lander — walk too far out and you can't walk back if the suit starts to fail. Wheels rewrote that math: Apollo 15 through 17 ranged kilometres from home, turning a single landing spot into a proper field area and letting geologists actually choose where to look. Building it was its own puzzle — it had to fold flat into a wedge on the side of the Lunar Module, unfold on the surface, then drive through abrasive dust and hundreds of degrees of temperature swing on wire-mesh wheels and battery power. It never went fast. It went far, and that was the whole point.
description: The Lunar Roving Vehicle — the first crewed rover. Three Apollos (15, 16, 17) used it to extend their surface exploration, covering up to 35.9 km per mission (Apollo 17 record). Built by Boeing and Delco; folded into the LM’s descent stage.
